**Verdict:** PASS
**Evidence:** The 3 new trait methods are all DEFAULT methods: `short_description()` → `self.description()` (`types/tool.rs:298`), `detailed_description()` → `None` (`:308`), `is_mcp_adapter()` → `false` (`:320`). `grep "impl AgentTool for" src/` yields exactly the 12 kernel production impls named in the claim (bash `:126`, edit `:48`, file×2 `:106`/`:256`, list `:48`, search `:59`, revert `:98`, prun `:137`, tool_help `:151`, sub_agent `:156`, openapi/adapter `:133`, mcp/tool_adapter `:106`) plus 4 `#[cfg(test)]` structs (tool.rs PlainTool/SplitTool, tool_help SchemaTool/McpShaped). `grep "fn is_mcp_adapter"` → the default (`:320`), the sole production override `mcp/tool_adapter.rs:136` returning `true` (rustdoc `:132-135`), and `tool_help.rs:470` which sits in the `#[cfg(test)]` `McpShaped` struct (`:460`). No other production impl needed a non-default override. `revert.rs:115` overrides `detailed_description()` — a deliberate split, NOT a compile-forced override. The 3 i-phi impls live in a separate submodule; they inherit unchanged by construction because all 3 methods are defaults (backcompat guaranteed structurally; orchestrator gate-2 build was GREEN).

### Claim 5a — DESIGN SCRUTINY: F1.a validator not auto-invoked
**Verdict:** PASS (coherent + documented) — advisory recommendation
**Evidence:** `validate_tool_registration` (`types/tool.rs:398`) is a public primitive returning `Err` on empty name / empty short / over-limit (hard-error = the DEFAULT return-stance, F1.a); missing `detailed_description()` is a non-fatal advisory via `tool_registration_warning` (`:426`). It is NOT force-invoked on the production hot path — the only call-sites are two `#[test]` fns (`revert.rs:339,358`), one of which (`kc05_default_tools_pass_registration_validation`, `:352`) is a CI-guard asserting every `default_tools()` built-in passes. This is a coherent joint realization of F1.a (hard-error is the default stance the helper enforces; the `revert_to_state` split was forced as a must-edit) + F2.b (not auto-invoking = the consumer owns the stance, per `[[feedback_phi_core_kernel_minimal]]`). It is adequately documented in ADR §D5.4 ("exposes the primitive but does not force-invoke it on the hot path — the enforcement stance is a consumer-overridable default") and rustdoc (`tool.rs:395-397`). **Judgment:** does not under-deliver F1.a; the "fails fast at agent-build/boot" promise is realized for kernel built-ins via the CI-guard test and for consumer tools via the exposed seam the i-phi follow-on wires at its agent-build. **Recommendation:** the i-phi per-agent follow-on MUST call `validate_tool_registration` at its agent-build to fully deliver the "fails fast at boot" user-visible promise for consumer-registered tools; consider adding a rustdoc example showing the recommended consumer wiring point so the seam is not missed.

### Claim 5b — DESIGN SCRUTINY: `is_mcp_adapter()` naming
**Verdict:** PASS (acceptable) — advisory recommendation
**Evidence:** MCP is a first-class kernel concept (`mcp/` module + `McpToolAdapter` kernel type at `tool_adapter.rs:106`), the name is honest and specific, and the rustdoc frames it as "a general transport-origin signal, not consumer policy" (`tool.rs:318-319`). The signal is consumed by `ProgressiveToolCatalog::engages` (`config.rs:443`). **Recommendation:** a more general framing (e.g. `carries_large_remote_schema()` / `has_deferred_schema()`) would (i) more precisely express what `engages()` actually keys on — schema-size / transport-origin, not "MCP-ness" per se — and (ii) let `OpenApiToolAdapter` (which similarly carries large generated schemas but currently inherits the `false` default) opt into the same magnification trigger without a second trait method. Advisory only; the specific name is acceptable as shipped given MCP is first-class and the rustdoc documents the intent.
